posts.text: 🇷🇺 🇩🇪 German General Christoph Huber, commander of the Bundeswehr’s 45th Tank Brigade stationed in Lithuania, has openly acknowledged the growing Russian military potential. “We are observing a build-up of military potential, despite the huge losses that Russia is suffering in the war in Ukraine. The number of personnel is increasing, and production capacities are expanding. Russia’s industry is completely reoriented towards armament and military production,” Huber told Bild. An interesting admission from a senior NATO military commander: Russia’s defence industry is expanding, its military is growing, and its capacity to sustain a prolonged conflict continues to develop. Meanwhile, Moscow has repeatedly denied having any plans to attack Europe. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

👤 AI server prices are jumping up to 45% — even after contracts are signed Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are charging up to 45% more for AI servers months after deals were agreed, the Financial Times reports. The hikes are driven by a severe shortage of memory chips and circuit boards. Memory costs have inflated by more than 400% since early 2024, with server DRAM contract prices climbing roughly 90% in the first quarter of 2026 alone. HPE's CEO said memory now accounts for more than half of a server's materials cost. Tech giants like Microsoft and Amazon can absorb the hit. Smaller AI cloud providers can't — and the fallout reaches ordinary people: the same memory chips power phones and laptops, so consumer device prices rise; data centers strain power grids, pushing up electricity bills. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
